## Short answer: no, it doesn't

`crimes scan --format json` fires `missing_agent_context` on this repo:

```
crime_00018  Missing Agent Context   medium   confidence 0.90   agent_risk 0.53
  - no AGENTS.md found at repo root
  - no CLAUDE.md found at repo root
  - no .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md present
  - no .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md present
  - package.json declares bin(s): tsup, tsup-node — agents have no way to discover commands
```

It's a repo-level finding, so the `file` field (`assets/cjs_shims.js`) is just an anchor — the subject is the repo root, not that file.

## Why it matters here specifically

The consequence isn't abstract. The other 86 findings describe exactly what an uninstructed agent will walk into:

**1. It won't know which files are load-bearing.** `src/utils.ts` has 18 importers (425 lines, `crime_00028`/`crime_00030`), `src/plugin.ts` has 10 with a 29-file blast radius (`crime_00015`), `src/log.ts` has 9 with a 30-file blast radius (`crime_00049`). An agent asked to "clean up utils" will restructure a module that a third of the repo depends on, because nothing told it not to.

**2. It can't discover the commands.** The package ships two binaries (`tsup`, `tsup-node`) and the scan explicitly flags that there's no discoverable entry point. An agent will guess at how to build, test, and typecheck — and guessing wrong on a build tool means it validates its change against the wrong thing.

**3. A green test run is not evidence.** 26 `weak_test_signal` findings — 12 tests with **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls (`test/example.test.ts`, `test/experimental-dts.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`, `test/index.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`, `test/tsconfig.test.ts`) and 14 more that only use weak matchers. An agent that runs the suite, sees it pass, and reports success has proven the code ran, not that behaviour is intact. This is the single most dangerous gap, and it's exactly the kind of thing only a context file can communicate.

**4. Edits will land in bodies too big to hold in context.** `build` is 293 lines (`crime_00008`), `runEsbuild` 237 (`crime_00001`), `main` 153 (`crime_00003`). Agents editing one section of these routinely miss interactions in another — and `build`/`buildAll`/`getRollupConfig` are additionally flagged as `name_behavior_mismatch`: safe-sounding names that mutate state.

The finding is `effort: small` / `risk: low`. It's the cheapest item in the whole report and it's the one that changes how every *other* finding gets handled.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

Repo root, `AGENTS.md`. The detector looks for the file's presence, but a stub that says nothing useful clears the check without buying anything — so this is scoped to the minimum that's actually load-bearing:

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

tsup — a TypeScript/JS bundler. Ships two binaries: `tsup` and `tsup-node`.

## Commands

- Install: `pnpm install`            <!-- verify against package.json -->
- Build:   `pnpm build`
- Test:    `pnpm test`
- Types:   `pnpm typecheck`
- Lint:    `pnpm lint`

Run build + test before proposing any change. Tests shell out to real
builds and are slow — expect minutes, not seconds.

## Layout

- `src/index.ts`         — public API and orchestration (`build`, `buildAll`, `startWatcher`)
- `src/cli-main.ts`      — CLI argument handling
- `src/esbuild/`         — esbuild pipeline and plugins (postcss, svelte, swc)
- `src/rollup.ts`        — .d.ts bundling via rollup
- `src/tsc.ts`, `src/api-extractor.ts` — declaration emit paths
- `src/utils.ts`, `src/log.ts` — shared helpers, imported nearly everywhere
- `test/`                — integration tests; `test/utils.ts` is shared harness

## Load-bearing files — read importers before editing

`src/utils.ts` (18 importers), `src/plugin.ts` (10), `src/log.ts` (9),
`test/utils.ts` (9). Prefer additive changes here. Do not restructure or
rename exports in these files as part of an unrelated task.

## Testing caveat — read this before trusting a green run

Parts of the suite assert weakly or not at all: several tests in
`test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`,
`test/tsconfig.test.ts`, and `test/experimental-dts.test.ts` contain no
assertions. **A passing suite does not prove your change is safe.** If you
touch behaviour those tests nominally cover, add a real assertion rather
than relying on the existing one.

## Conventions

- Async I/O is preferred in new code; existing `*Sync` calls in
  `src/utils.ts` and `src/fs.ts` are legacy, don't add more.
- `build`, `buildAll`, `getRollupConfig`, and `buildStart` perform side
  effects (file removal, logger setup) despite their names. Don't assume purity.
- Don't reformat or reorganise files you aren't otherwise changing.

## Out of scope without asking

Changing output file naming/extensions, the public options shape in
`src/index.ts`, or the dts pipeline — these are user-visible contracts.
```

Two things to verify before committing it: the actual script names in `package.json` (I've marked them as placeholders — the scan reports bins, not scripts), and whether `pnpm` is the right package manager for this repo.

Re-running `crimes scan --format json` after adding it should drop `crime_00018` and take the report from 87 to 86 findings, with `medium` going 38 → 37.
